findings.title: 28 classes of explorer.module.css belong to the former library page and no component uses them
findings.evidence: A CSS module class is only reachable as explorer / shared.<name> or explorer / shared["<name>"] in a file that imports explorer.module.css; a script listed every class of explorer.module.css, every importer and its alias, and every dynamic explorer / shared[...] index. Importers: entry.tsx, new-view.tsx, organisation.tsx and page.tsx (alias explorer), facet-page.tsx (alias shared); no dynamic index. Used classes: lead, primaryAction, count, empty, crumbs, eyebrow, facetStrip, facetChip, panel, reference. Unused classes with the line of their first rule: page (1), libraryHeader (6), toolbar (25), tabs (33, 39, 42-57), tabsAction (61), filters (75, 81), search (82, 90), group (97), groupTitle (102, 112), threadList (115), threadRow (124-135), threadLink (138, 149), threadHead (152), threadTitle (157), threadSummary (161), threadMeta (169), metaStrong (176), framework (180), pill (187), active (198), frozen (202), completed (206), cardGrid (210), card (215-237), cardTitle (241), activeThread (244), header (265), timeline (311-330), and the whole @media (max-width: 760px) block at lines 334-353, which only styles unused classes. Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/: no file reaches these classes through explorer.module.css. Acceptance tests select by [class*='stepName'], [class*='icon'], [class*='tipDate'] and [class*='tipReason'] only, none of which matches these names. The thread list of the entry page is now rendered by thread-rows.tsx with entry.module.css.
findings.action: Delete the rules of the 28 unused classes and the @media (max-width: 760px) block from explorer.module.css; keep lead, primaryAction, count, empty, crumbs, eyebrow, facetStrip, facetChip, panel and reference.
findings.riskReason: CSS module class names are hashed, so no element can carry these classes unless a component names them, and none does; the remaining rules are untouched.

Rules concerned: .mark (158-161), .checkItem .mark (162-168), .satisfied/.failed/.actionable/.running .mark (200-212), and the reduced-motion block (228-232). findings.action: Delete the .mark, .checkItem .mark and '.<tone> .mark' rules and the reduced-motion block that only stops the .running .mark animation; keep styles[tone] on the row, which .blocked .checkName still needs.
findings.riskReason: No element in plan-views.tsx carries the mark class; the rules can match nothing.

findings.title: threadPresentation in thread-status.ts computes a tone that nothing reads
findings.evidence: The only caller of threadPresentation is threadStatus in the same file, which returns .label only. Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/ for threadPresentation: only thread-status.ts; for threadStatus: entry.tsx (lines 100 and 304) and new-view.tsx (line 41), all reading the returned label. The tones active, frozen and completed were the classes of the former explorer.module.css pills, which no component uses any more.
findings.action: Drop the tone field and merge threadPresentation into threadStatus, which returns the label for each state.
findings.riskReason: No reader of tone exists; the labels returned by threadStatus are unchanged.

findings.title: thread-status.ts repeats the thread state labels that threadState in visual-language.tsx already defines
findings.evidence: Both switch over the thread state and return the same English labels: In progress, Open, Paused and Completed, with the same error for an unknown state. threadStatus feeds the state filter of entry.tsx and the summary of new-view.tsx; threadState feeds the state pills (ThreadStatePill). Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/: no other definition of these labels in ui/.
findings.action: Make entry.tsx and new-view.tsx use threadState(thread, state === "IN_PROGRESS").label from visual-language.tsx (or a small wrapper exported from it) and delete thread-status.ts.
findings.riskReason: threadState takes the ACTIVE state plus an atWork flag while threadStatus takes the synthetic IN_PROGRESS state; the mapping must keep the filter labels identical, and the filter of entry.tsx is covered by browser tests only.

findings.title: FormPage in organisation.tsx receives a go prop and calls useI18n without reading either
findings.evidence: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters in trust-extension/extensions/corpus reports exactly two errors: organisation.tsx(22,3) 'go' is declared but its value is never read, and organisation.tsx(32,9) 't' is declared but its value is never read. Both callers (lines 94 and 221) pass go={go}.
findings.action: Remove the go prop from FormPage (destructuring, type and the two go={go} at the call sites) and the unused const { t } = useI18n() in FormPage.
findings.riskReason: The compiler proves neither value is read; the call sites keep go for their own use.

findings.title: The French entry "A completed thread keeps its corpus." of i18n.tsx is used by no t() call

location.text: "A completed thread keeps its corpus.": "Un thread terminé garde son corpus.",

findings.evidence: A script evaluated the fr catalogue (453 keys) and searched every other ui/*.ts(x) file for each key as a string literal; it also listed every t() call with a non-literal argument and resolved the conditional literals and the tables behind them (GROUPING_LABELS, KIND_LABELS, GROUP_LABELS, segmentLabels, eventLabels, item.kind, `kind|${result.kind}`, state.label). Every other key is used. This key matches only the server refusal in trust-extension/extensions/corpus/domain.mjs (line 1109) and its server acceptance test; no t() call in ui/ passes a server message variable that could resolve to it (the only free-variable call, t(notice) in interaction.tsx, receives the single literal set in plan-input.tsx). No t() call in ui/ uses a key absent from the French catalogue.
findings.action: Delete the entry from the fr catalogue.
findings.riskReason: No t() call can reach the key; the server message is unaffected.

findings.title: new-view.tsx names styles.primary, a class entry.module.css does not define
findings.evidence: A script listed every <alias>.<name> reference of the ui/*.tsx files and compared it with the classes of the imported module: the only reference to a missing class is styles.primary in new-view.tsx, where styles is entry.module.css. Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/ for '.primary' in ui/*.css: none (explorer.module.css has .primaryAction, which is a different class). The class attribute therefore renders as undefined and the save button of the new view has no class.
findings.action: Remove className={styles.primary} from the save button of new-view.tsx.
findings.riskReason: The reference already resolves to undefined, so removing it renders the same button.

findings.title: The global class corpus-thread-list set in thread-rows.tsx has no stylesheet, script or test that uses it
findings.evidence: Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/, and the whole repository (excluding node_modules, dist and bundle) for corpus-thread-list as a word: the only match is the className cited here. No .css file (module or global, including :global() selectors) and no querySelector or Playwright locator names it. Global corpus-* classes that tests do use (corpus-app, corpus-thread, corpus-thread-number, corpus-thread-status, corpus-thread-card, corpus-lifecycle, corpus-state-pill, corpus-markdown) are not recorded.
findings.action: Remove corpus-thread-list from the className, keeping the module class.
findings.riskReason: No rule, script or test selects the class; only an external user stylesheet could, and none is known.
